writeup.1: Precision in the Wild is the second collection PUMA Golf and Realtree have made together, ten pieces released on Monday. The interesting part is how differently it behaves from the first one.
writeup.2: The first drop, in February 2025, was a spectacle. It ran in Realtree Edge, Deep Forest and Rickie Orange, and it arrived on Rickie Fowler head to toe on the Thursday of the WM Phoenix Open, the rowdiest stage in professional golf and chosen deliberately. The second arrived on a Monday in late August in Dusty Olive and Alpine Snow, with no tournament and no player attached to it.
writeup.3: What it has instead is a new pattern. Realtree Legacy was made for the company’s fortieth anniversary, and it is the first pattern co-designed by founder Bill Jordan and his son Tyler. It takes the dark bark structure of the Original pattern and warms it into browns and warm greys where Original ran cool, with segmented bark lines and drop shadows doing the depth work. On the fleece vest it looks like a hunting layer. On the spikeless HELSINKI G runner it reads as a shoe you would keep on off the course.
writeup.4: PUMA has form here. The Volition America line has carried camo golf shirts for years in patriotic red, white and blue for Folds of Honor. Realtree gives PUMA the same visual language with outdoor-industry provenance behind it, which is the argument PUMA itself makes: plenty of golf brands have dabbled in camo without much of it meaning anything.
writeup.5: All ten pieces run from $40 to $190, every image is PUMA’s own, and everything is in stock.
